subject: SIG evidence: access-rights vs. audit-log granularity
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <psharma@cygnus-audit.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: evidence@novopulse.com
Date: 2028-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG evidence: access-rights vs. audit-log granularity

Hi Laura / Kimberly,

We're preparing Novopulse's SIG v2 pack and need clarification on the audit log granularity for access-rights questions. Specifically, the customer is asking for evidence showing: 

- who changed a user's roles/permissions (user + admin actor)
- timestamp and source (UI vs API) for each change
- whether changes are reversible or have an audit-delivery manifest

Couple of follow-ups: 
1) What exact admin actions are captured (create/delete/role-change/permission-grant/ssh/key rotation)?
2) How long do you retain those admin-action events by default and for enterprise tenants?
3) Export options: can you produce a time-bounded, signed manifest (JSONL or Parquet) with checksums and HMAC for chain-of-custody?

We need a short reply today if possible so we can finalize the SIG evidence matrix. Also let us know if you have a sample export so Novopulse's security team can validate ingestion.

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
Senior Auditor, Cygnus Audit LLP
psharma@cygnus-audit.com
+1 (415) 555-0182


From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <psharma@cygnus-audit.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG evidence: access-rights vs. audit-log granularity

Priya — thanks for the clear ask. High level answers below; Kimberly and Marissa are copied for specifics and export mechanics.

Short answers: 
- Captured actions: create/update/delete for users, role assignments, permission grants/revokes, API key creation/revocation, OAuth client grants, and changes to RBAC policies.
- Source metadata: every admin event includes actor id, actor role (admin/system), IP (if available), request method (UI/API), and request id.
- Retention: default admin-activity retention is 1 year; for enterprise Tenants we support configurable retention up to 7 years via Dedicated/Private plans (contracted).
- Exports: we can produce time-bounded JSONL or Parquet exports with a signed manifest and SHA256 checksums. We support S3 PUT with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) and provide an HMAC-signed manifest for chain-of-custody.

I'll defer to Kimberly for field-level examples and to Marissa for scheduling the sample handoff. Attaching the export options brief (redwood-audit-export-options.pdf) and a small sample manifest (sample_admin_audit_manifest.jsonl) for Novopulse to inspect.

Next steps: 
- Kimberly: could you paste the field list and an example record?
- Marissa: can you propose a 30-minute window tomorrow to walk Novopulse through the sample?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Sharma <psharma@cygnus-audit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-04T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG evidence: access-rights vs. audit-log granularity

Thanks Laura — field-level detail below (sample JSONL line included). Notes on sampling/redaction and formats follow.

Fields we capture for each admin event (example purposes):
- event_id (uuid)
- recorded_at (ISO8601)
- tenant_id
- actor_user_id
- actor_display_name
- actor_role
- target_user_id
- action (role_add | role_remove | permission_update | api_key_create | api_key_revoke | rbac_change)
- source (ui | api | cli)
- request_ip
- request_user_agent
- request_id
- changes (JSON blob: before/after where applicable)
- outcome (success | failure)
- retention_bucket (default | longterm_contract)

Sample JSONL line (single-line):
{"event_id":"e7b6b2c4-9c2a-4f3b-8a4c-9a1d2b1f7c80","recorded_at":"2028-04-30T22:14:03Z","tenant_id":"novopulse-prod","actor_user_id":"laura.b@redwood","actor_display_name":"Laura Bennett","actor_role":"Compliance Admin","target_user_id":"j.santos@novopulse.com","action":"role_add","source":"ui","request_ip":"34.120.45.9","request_user_agent":"Mozilla/5.0","request_id":"req-9a12f3","changes":{"before":[],"after":["billing:viewer"]},"outcome":"success","retention_bucket":"default"}

Export options and delivery:
- Formats: JSONL (line-delimited), Parquet (columnar) — both include identical fields.
- Integrity: each export directory includes a manifest.json (signed) and per-file SHA256 checksums. If requested, we append an HMAC signature using the customer's KMS-wrapped key.
- Delivery: options are S3 (pre-signed PUT with SSE-KMS), SFTP push, or secure HTTPS download behind a single-use token.
- Sampling & PII: for SIG/CAIQ deliverables we provide a full export for the requested time range. If Novopulse requests PII redaction, we deliver a redacted export plus an attestation of the redaction mapping.

Retention notes: 
- Non-enterprise (hosted): 1 year (admin activity), 90 days (runtime traces).
- Dedicated/Private: configurable, contractual retention up to 7 years; we can do on-request deep-archive exports to customer S3 with WORM if required.

If those fields look good, I can prepare a 24-hour sample slice for Novopulse to load.

--
Kimberly Park
Sr. Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Deliverables on the call:

- export options brief (pdf) and redaction checklist
- a short runbook describing how Novopulse can validate checksums and verify HMAC signature with KMS flow

I'll send the S3 link + one-time token in a follow-up before the call. Let me know if you need the export in Parquet instead.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference
